concepts.title: Mendel's Experiments and the Rules of Inheritance

questions.a: Crossing tall and dwarf pea plants: F1 all tall, F2 shows 3 tall : 1 dwarf, proving traits are carried by discrete factors.

questions.q: What did Mendel conclude from F2 ratios?
questions.a: Traits exist as pairs of factors; a recessive factor can be masked in F1 but reappear in F2.

questions.q: Why did Mendel choose pea plants?
questions.a: Clear contrasting traits, self and cross-pollination are easy, and short life cycle with many offspring.

concepts.title: How Traits Are Expressed - Genes and DNA

questions.a: On chromosomes inside the nucleus of every cell.

questions.q: How does a gene express itself as a trait?
questions.a: It directs production of a protein or enzyme, which then brings about the visible trait.

questions.q: Why are fathers not responsible for the sex of a child?
questions.a: Fathers contribute either X or Y chromosome; the mother always contributes X, so the father's gamete decides the sex.

questions.q: What chromosomes do human males and females carry?
How is the sex of a baby determined?
questions.a: If the father's sperm carries X, the child is a girl (XX); if Y, a boy (XY).

questions.q: In some animals like turtles, what decides sex?
questions.a: Incubation temperature of the eggs, not chromosomes.
